content:
I'm writing this article right now, and I'm about to head off on a short trip up north. Every time I leave home, there are a few essential devices in my smart home system that I rely on completely to make sure everything runs smoothly. Just a reminder: to control your devices remotely and access all the features below, you'll need a dedicated Apple Home home hub, such as the Apple TV 4K or HomePod.

The HomeKit Weekly series focuses on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Automating an outdoor watering system

Where I live, the heat is absolutely unbearable. I think when you're away from home, you either hope for rain or you have to water your plants yourself. If you're travelling in the summer, automatic watering is definitely one of the simplest and most practical smart home applications. If you've ever come back from a week away only to find a patch of grass or a few potted plants completely dead, you'll definitely understand what I'm talking about. There are plenty of smart products on the market that connect directly to your hose, allowing you to manually turn on sprinklers or set up automation based on specific times and local weather conditions.

Walk into a comfortable temperature as soon as you get home

Coming back from a long trip and finding the whole house hot and stuffy, with the air conditioner taking forever to cool down, is absolutely the worst experience. On the other hand, running the air conditioner continuously to maintain the temperature of an empty house is a complete waste of money. With a smart thermostat that supports Apple Home, you can remotely adjust the air conditioner to your preferred temperature the night before. I've been doing this for years. I prefer to turn it on in the evening, so the unit takes advantage of the coolest part of the day to bring the temperature down. This saves money and reduces unnecessary wear on the air conditioner.

Automating lights to create the impression that someone's home

One of the most traditional security tricks is to leave a few lights on so the property looks occupied. The problem is, if the same light stays on day and night, it's actually a dead giveaway that no one's home. This is exactly where Apple Home comes in handy. By automating several of your main lights, you can control them manually from afar or set random schedules, which can truly create the effect of someone moving around the house.

  • SYLVANIA SMART+ Bluetooth Soft White A19 LED Bulb
  • OREiN Matter Smart Bulb
  • Linkind Matter Smart Bulb
  • Kasa Smart Plug Mini
  • Best Connect Matter Smart Plug
  • Linkind Matter Smart Plug

Use HomeKit cameras to monitor your home

When I'm travelling, I definitely don't want to be thinking about my home all the time, but I do want to know if anything's going on. In fact, last year I was able to catch a small issue while I was on the road thanks to an alert. That's precisely why I trust HomeKit Secure Video so much. I've installed a few cameras outside to keep an eye on the surroundings of my home. With HomeKit Secure Video, all the recorded footage is securely stored on iCloud+, and since I also use several Apple TVs as hubs, I can easily check live footage and recordings from anywhere, as long as I have a network connection.

Conclusion

Summer is truly a great time for travelling, but at the same time, your home needs a bit more care because of the extreme heat. With the right Apple Home setup, you can keep your lawn well-watered, enjoy a cool temperature as soon as you walk through the door, set your lights to a varied schedule, and check your camera's live feed anytime, anywhere. The above is exactly the setup I use when I'm away for work or family trips, and they really make travelling so much easier.
